gen-vast-shadow-gf-noto-sans-sc: Noto Sans SC keeps its curves unfinished, chalk-like arcs that stop well short of closing, with ascenders barely rising above the lowercase. Vast Shadow, by contrast, is cut stencil-flat at a single width, so over a full page the body feels light and unhurried beside it.
gen-vast-shadow-gf-noto-sans-sharada: Vast Shadow looks cut from flat stock, every stroke the same width, with no thick-thin pulse to pull the eye along. Noto Sans Sharada settles into a long read easily, its open c forms and bulky lowercase keeping the lines relaxed and friendly.
gen-vast-shadow-gf-noto-sans-siddham:
Vast Shadow looks like bent wire, tall and vintage.

Noto Sans Siddham counters with a large central band and an s whose ends hang far from the spine, so a longer passage feels approachable and contemporary.
gen-vast-shadow-gf-noto-sans-sinhala: Flat, stencil-bold and a bit retro: Vast Shadow even gives its t a crossbar and stem of one width. Noto Sans Sinhala lays a thick, dark stripe of lowercase through every line, and its curve endings stay well apart, so a long read stays steady.
gen-vast-shadow-gf-noto-sans-soyombo: Tall, flat and vintage, Vast Shadow keeps one unbroken line weight from terminals to junctions. But Noto Sans Soyombo has a sizable x-height and wide, unclosed curves, so it can be set at a modest size on screen and still read comfortably.
gen-vast-shadow-gf-noto-sans-sundanese: Vast Shadow's most striking trait is a line that never swells or tapers, giving its tall, widely spaced letters a vintage stencil look. And Noto Sans Sundanese sits beneath it with open-mouthed e crossbars and little gap between x-height and cap height, making a tidy, clean counterweight.
gen-vast-shadow-gf-noto-sans-sunuwar: Noto Sans Sunuwar leaves daylight in its curves, like a rope's open bight, with short ascender stems on tall lowercase bodies. But Vast Shadow's n has an arch and stem that match, so a longer passage in the body feels approachable beside that stencil-like heading.
gen-vast-shadow-gf-noto-sans-syloti-nagr:
Vast Shadow has a sign-painter's stencil flatness, with every stroke the same.

Noto Sans Syloti Nagri brings short ascenders, a tall x-height and an a whose lower bowl opens up, so a longer passage reads in a clean, professional way.
gen-vast-shadow-gf-noto-sans-syriac:
Flat, tall and vintage, with plenty of room around each letter.

Vast Shadow's unvarying line weight is the loud half of the pair, and Noto Sans Syriac, with bowls like blown glass bulbs and wide, easy s turns, is its approachable counterpart.
gen-vast-shadow-gf-noto-sans-syriac-east:
Noto Sans Syriac Eastern reads tall and friendly, its lowercase towering over small caps.

Vast Shadow is best at grabbing attention, with diagonals as thick as its uprights, while the body font is best at quietly carrying text, its curve endings never crowding each other.
